taxYearRuns: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2026 (calendar-year taxpayers; returns filed in 2027)
jurisdiction: United States — federal only. State income tax, state unemployment insurance and local taxes are out of scope.
refreshRule: Re-verify when the IRS publishes the tax-year-2027 inflation adjustments (normally mid/late October), the 2027 retirement-plan limits (normally early/mid November) and when SSA publishes the 2027 COLA/wage base (normally mid-October; Federal Register notice follows in late October/early November). Until then these 2026 figures are final.
verificationMethod: Every figure was read on verifiedDate from the primary document named in its `source` (IRS Revenue Procedure / Notice PDFs and irs.gov pages fetched with curl, User-Agent databutler-curation/1.0; all returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-03). The `quote` field reproduces the sentence or table row the value was taken from. `previous` values come from the 2025 counterpart document named in `previousSource` or from the same page where it states the prior-year figure. Figures were never written from memory and were not copied from any third-party calculator or from the LifeByNumbers app.py — disagreements with app.py are listed in NOTES.md.
licence: Works of the United States federal government (IRS, SSA, Federal Register) are in the public domain under 17 U.S.C. § 105. Figures are reproduced with their source URL; no third-party content is included.

income-tax.title: Federal income tax — rate schedules and standard deduction, tax year 2026
income-tax.scope: Individuals; taxable income after deductions. Schedules per § 1(j)(2)(A)–(D) as adjusted by Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.01 (which also reflects OBBBA changes).

previous.quote: Section 63(c)(7) as amended by the OBBBA provides the standard deduction amounts … for any taxable year beginning in 2025 as follows: … Unmarried Individuals … $15,750

figures.quote: § 3.14(1) … Heads of Households (§ 1(j)(2)(B)) $24,150

figures.label: Additional standard deduction for aged (65+) or blind, § 63(f) — per qualifying condition, married or surviving spouse
figures.quote: § 3.14(3) Aged or blind. For taxable years beginning in 2026, the additional standard deduction amount under § 63(f) for the aged or the blind is $1,650.

previous.quote: the additional standard deduction amount under § 63(f) for the aged or the blind is $1,600

figures.label: Additional standard deduction for aged (65+) or blind, § 63(f) — per qualifying condition, unmarried and not a surviving spouse

figures.label: Standard deduction for an individual claimable as a dependent, § 63(c)(5) — cannot exceed the greater of this amount or $450 plus earned income
figures.quote: § 3.14(2) Dependent. … cannot exceed the greater of (1) $1,350, or (2) the sum of $450 and the individual's earned income.

figures.label: Top marginal rate
figures.quote: For tax year 2026, the top tax rate remains 37% for individual single taxpayers with incomes greater than $640,600 ($768,700 for married couples filing jointly).

social-security.title: Social Security (OASDI) payroll tax — wage base and rates, 2026
social-security.scope: Employees and employers (FICA). Self-employed pay both halves (12.4%) under SECA.

figures.label: OASDI contribution and benefit base (Social Security wage base)
figures.quote: The OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026.

previous.quote: Because $184,500 exceeds the current base amount of $176,100, the OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for 2026.

corroboration.quote: The social security wage base limit is $184,500.

figures.label: Social Security tax rate — employee share
figures.quote: The rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% each for the employer and employee.

corroboration.quote: The current tax rate for Social Security is 6.2% for the employer and 6.2% for the employee, or 12.4% total.

figures.label: Social Security tax rate — employer share
figures.quote: The rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% each for the employer and employee.

figures.label: Cost-of-living adjustment to benefits effective December 2025 (paid January 2026)
figures.quote: Under title II of the Social Security Act (Act), there will be a 2.8 percent cost-of-living increase in Social Security benefits effective December 2025.

figures.label: Earnings required for one quarter of coverage
figures.quote: The earnings required for a quarter of coverage in 2026 is $1,890.

medicare.title: Medicare (HI) payroll tax — rate and Additional Medicare Tax thresholds, 2026
medicare.scope: No wage base limit. Additional Medicare Tax thresholds are statutory (not indexed) and apply to the sum of wages, RRTA compensation and self-employment income.

figures.label: Medicare tax rate — employee share (employer pays the same)
figures.quote: The Medicare tax rate is 1.45% each for the employee and employer, unchanged from 2025. There is no wage base limit for Medicare tax.

corroboration.quote: The current rate for Medicare is 1.45% for the employer and 1.45% for the employee, or 2.9% total.

figures.label: Additional Medicare Tax rate (employee only; no employer match)
figures.quote: The rate is 0.9 percent.

figures.label: Additional Medicare Tax threshold — Married filing jointly
figures.quote: Married filing jointly $250,000

figures.label: Additional Medicare Tax threshold — Married filing separately
figures.quote: Married filing separate $125,000

figures.label: Additional Medicare Tax threshold — Single, Head of household, Qualifying widow(er)
figures.quote: Single $200,000; Head of household (with qualifying person) $200,000; Qualifying widow(er) with dependent child $200,000

figures.label: Employer withholding threshold for Additional Medicare Tax (per employer, regardless of filing status)
figures.quote: Employers are responsible for withholding the 0.9% Additional Medicare tax on an individual's wages paid in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year, without regard to filing status.

retirement.title: Retirement plan and IRA contribution limits, 2026
retirement.scope: Cost-of-living adjusted limits under § 415(d) and related sections; effective 1 January 2026.

figures.label: 401(k) / 403(b) / governmental 457(b) / TSP elective deferral limit, § 402(g)(1)
figures.quote: The limitation under section 402(g)(1) on the exclusion for elective deferrals described in section 402(g)(3), which includes elective deferrals made to the Thrift Savings Plan, is increased from $23,500 to $24,500.

figures.label: Catch-up contribution, age 50 and over, § 414(v)(2)(B)(i)
figures.quote: The limitation under section 414(v)(2)(B)(i) for catch-up contributions to an applicable employer plan … that generally applies for individuals aged 50 or over is increased from $7,500 to $8,000.

figures.label: Higher catch-up contribution for individuals who attain age 60, 61, 62 or 63 in 2026, § 414(v)(2)(E)(i) (SECURE 2.0)
figures.quote: The limitation under section 414(v)(2)(E)(i) for catch-up contributions … that applies for individuals who attain age 60, 61, 62, or 63 in 2026 remains $11,250.

figures.label: Wage threshold above which catch-up contributions must be Roth, § 414(v)(7)(A) (based on prior-year FICA wages)
figures.quote: The Roth catch-up wage threshold for 2025, which under section 414(v)(7)(A) is used to determine whether an individual's catch-up contributions … for 2026 must be designated as Roth contributions, is increased from $145,000 to $150,000.

figures.label: Defined contribution plan annual additions limit, § 415(c)(1)(A)
figures.quote: The limitation for defined contribution plans under section 415(c)(1)(A) is increased in 2026 from $70,000 to $72,000.

figures.label: Annual compensation limit, § 401(a)(17)
figures.quote: The annual compensation limitation under sections 401(a)(17), 404(l), 408(k)(3)(C), and 408(k)(6)(D)(ii) is increased from $350,000 to $360,000.

figures.label: IRA contribution limit (traditional + Roth combined), § 219(b)(5)(A)
figures.quote: The deductible amount under section 219(b)(5)(A), which limits the amount of an individual's deductible qualified retirement contributions for a taxable year is increased from $7,000 to $7,500.

figures.label: IRA catch-up contribution, age 50 and over, § 219(b)(5)(B)(ii) (indexed from 2024 under SECURE 2.0)
figures.quote: The deductible amount pursuant to section 219(b)(5)(B)(ii) for individuals who have attained age 50 before the close of the taxable year is increased from $1,000 to $1,100.

figures.label: SIMPLE IRA / SIMPLE 401(k) salary reduction limit, § 408(p)(2)(E)(i)(III)
figures.quote: … salary reduction contributions under a SIMPLE retirement account or elective contributions under a SIMPLE 401(k) plan is increased from $16,500 to $17,000.

figures.label: Highly compensated employee threshold, § 414(q)(1)(B)
figures.quote: The threshold used in the definition of "highly compensated employee" under section 414(q)(1)(B) remains $160,000.

hsa.title: Health Savings Accounts — contribution limits and HDHP definition, calendar year 2026
hsa.scope: § 223. Catch-up for age 55+ ($1,000) is statutory and not in the Rev. Proc.

figures.label: HSA annual contribution limit — self-only HDHP coverage, § 223(b)(2)(A)
figures.quote: For calendar year 2026, the annual limitation on deductions under § 223(b)(2)(A) for an individual with self-only coverage under a high deductible health plan is $4,400.

previous.quote: For calendar year 2025, the annual limitation … self-only coverage … is $4,300.

figures.label: HSA annual contribution limit — family HDHP coverage, § 223(b)(2)(B)
figures.quote: For calendar year 2026, the annual limitation on deductions under § 223(b)(2)(B) for an individual with family coverage under a high deductible health plan is $8,750.

previous.quote: … family coverage under a high deductible health plan is $8,550.

figures.label: HDHP minimum annual deductible — self-only
figures.quote: a "high deductible health plan" is defined under § 223(c)(2)(A) as a health plan with an annual deductible that is not less than $1,700 for self-only coverage or $3,400 for family coverage

figures.label: HDHP minimum annual deductible — family
figures.quote: … not less than $1,700 for self-only coverage or $3,400 for family coverage

figures.label: HDHP maximum annual out-of-pocket (deductibles, co-payments, other amounts, not premiums) — self-only
figures.quote: … the annual out-of-pocket expenses … do not exceed $8,500 for self-only coverage or $17,000 for family coverage.

figures.label: HDHP maximum annual out-of-pocket — family
figures.quote: … do not exceed $8,500 for self-only coverage or $17,000 for family coverage.

figures.label: Excepted benefit HRA maximum newly available amount, plan years beginning in 2026
figures.quote: For plan years beginning in 2026, the maximum amount that may be made newly available for the plan year for an excepted benefit HRA under § 54.9831-1(c)(3)(viii) is $2,200.

estate-gift.title: Estate, gift and generation-skipping transfer tax — exclusion amounts, calendar year 2026
estate-gift.scope: Federal transfer taxes. The basic exclusion amount is unified across estate and gift tax (§ 2010(c), § 2505).

figures.label: Estate and gift tax basic exclusion amount, § 2010(c)(3) (set by OBBBA § 70106 for 2026; indexed from 2027)
figures.quote: Section 70106 of the OBBBA amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for calendar year 2026. … The basic exclusion amount will be adjusted for inflation for calendar year 2027 and future years.

previous.quote: Estates of decedents who die during 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000, up from a total of $13,990,000 for estates of decedents who died in 2025.

figures.label: Generation-skipping transfer tax exemption, § 2631(c)
figures.quote: For calendar year 2026, the generation-skipping transfer exemption amount under § 2631(c) is equal to $15,000,000.

figures.label: Annual exclusion for gifts, § 2503(b)
figures.quote: § 3.42(1) For calendar year 2026, the first $19,000 of gifts to any person (other than gifts of future interests in property) are not included in the total amount of taxable gifts under § 2503 made during that year.

previous.quote: For calendar year 2025, the first $19,000 of gifts to any person … are not included

figures.label: Annual exclusion for gifts to a spouse who is not a U.S. citizen, § 2523(i)(2)
figures.quote: the annual exclusion for gifts to a spouse who is not a citizen of the United States increases to $194,000 for calendar year 2026, up $4,000 from calendar year 2025.
